Harmful variations cause individuals less capable in the struggle for survival, while useful ones are quite significant that help the organism fit the environment. Useless variations are not significant from an evolutionary point of view. Beneficial variations are passed down to the next generation, making them better suited to their environment. d) Natural selection (Survival of the Fittest): The organisms which are provided with useful or favorable variation would survive because they are fit to face environmental challenges, whereas unfits get destroyed. The organisms which sort out useful variations are said to be the fittest. But it was unknown how only useful variations are sorted out by the organisms for which Darwin said that these variations are sorted out by nature. This is natural selection. Herbert Spencer first used the phrase 'survival of the fittest' for this phenomenon. e) Origin of species (Speciation): The useful variations acquired by organisms as result of natural selection are passed down to offsprings that become prominent over the generations. Improvements in the organisms in successive generations gradually diverged from their parents, resulting in the emergence of more adapted and better organized organisms which are identified as a new species. EXAMPLES OF NATURAL SELECTION a) Evolution of Giraffe Originally, there were giraffes with both short and long necks. With the scarcity of leaves on the lower branches of trees, they were forced to reach the higher branches favouring the survival of the long necked giraffes. This phased out the giraffes with short necks as they could not reach higher leaves. Thus, the giraffes with longer necks were selected by nature that survived and reproduced to the present day giraffes.

b. Resistance of mosquito to pesticides: Mosquitoes make people sick by spreading diseases like malaria. So, an insecticide called DDT (banned now) was used to kill mosquitoes effectively. But now, it is not effective because some mosquitoes have developed a special ability to survive the DDT. This shows how nature picks the mosquitoes that can survive and pass their abilities onto their offspring.

c. Industrial melanism: In Britain, peppered moths (Biston betularia) in industrial areas were of two types: light-colored and black (due to pigment melanin). Before industrial pollution, light-colored moths were common as they could blend with the surrounding pale tree trunks and protect themselves from their predators like birds. But with industrial
pollution, the color of tree trunks turned black making the light-colored moths conspicuous and visible to predators. This resulted in declination in their number but favoured blackcolored moths.

CRITICISM OF DARWINISM Darwin's theory of natural selection was widely accepted, given its logical basis and strong support. However, some objections were later raised: i. Darwinism lacked the knowledge of heredity and could not explain how variation occurred. ii. It could not justify the inheritance of small variations which are not useful in organisms. iii. It could not explain over specialization of some organs like elephant’s tusk and antlers of deer. iv. Darwin's theory explained survival of the fittest but not how the fittest initially emerged. v. It didn't account for the presence of vestigial organs. vi. The distinction between somatic and germinal variations was not addressed.
